assets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Production pixel-art furniture atlas 1 for RiftMon, a top-down Nintendo DS era monster RPG. Image 1 is the exact design and palette reference for existing furniture. Draw a strict grid of FOUR equal columns and 8 equal rows, generous fully transparent gutters. Each row shows ONE identical furniture design in four genuinely REDRAWN orientations, columns: front facing camera/down (0), right-facing (90), back-facing/up (180), left-facing (270). These are new perspective drawings, never rotated images: vertical surfaces remain vertical, top surfaces retain the same overhead perspective; legs still point down on screen. Right/left views reveal side panels; back view reveals plain backs. No isometric diamond floor. Maintain original object colors, forms and compact scale. Row order top to bottom: 1. table ronde en bois; 2. chaise en bois rouge; 3. canapé bleu deux places; 4. lit grenat avec oreiller blanc; 5. armoire chêne à deux portes; 6. bibliothèque pleine de livres; 7. miroir ovale sur pied; 8. tapis bleu rectangulaire. Crisp restrained low-resolution pixel art, dark single-pixel outlines, 3 or 4 flat shades per material. Each cell represents a logical 64x64 pixel sprite; maximum furniture extent 48x48 logical pixels, centered horizontally and bottom-aligned. A bed is 32px wide by48px tall when facing down/up; side bed is48px wide by32px tall. Tall cupboards keep their height in every view; do not squash side views. Rugs show a pattern rotated within a top-down floor plane, no standing upright. Keep every sprite completely inside its own cell with transparent margins, no overlaps or cutoffs. No text, no labels, no numbers, no borders, no scenery, no shadows outside sprite, no glow, no antialiasing or white fringe. Actual transparent background. Deliver exactly four views per row.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Create a replacement exit doorway sprite for the SOUTH wall of a top-down pixel-art RPG room. Image 1 provides the game's wooden architectural palette. This is an open passage leading DOWN out of the room, viewed from above; NOT a front-facing tall door on the north wall. Show two short timber jambs at the left and right, a low wooden threshold, a narrow dark downward passage between them, no overhead lintel across the opening, no roof panel, no ceiling, no raised platform. The player should clearly walk between the jambs onto the floor threshold and out of the room. Compact logical32x24 pixel tile, warm oak and dark blue shadows, dark crisp pixel outline, flat 3-tone shading, same simple handheld pixel art style. Isolated actual transparent background, no white fringes or stray pixels, no text. Keep the center passage clear.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the casino cabinet to edit. Keep its design, navy and burgundy body, brass edging, golden crown lamp, three reel window and right-hand lever. Redraw only the perspective: turn the cabinet about 30 degrees further toward the RIGHT side of the screen, so its deep LEFT side panel occupies roughly a third of its width and its front face is visibly narrower, seen from a top-down three-quarter view appropriate for an object standing against a room's left wall. It faces toward the center of the room (screen right and slightly down). Keep a vertical upright cabinet and its feet level, no tilt, no frontal wide rectangular face. Preserve the same compact simple low-resolution pixel-art style, hard dark outline, flat shades, no texture or glow. Actual transparent background, no white fringes or stray pixels, no new decor or labels.

Use case: style-transfer. Production pixel-art furniture sheet for the same RPG as image 1. Draw exactly TWO ROWS and FOUR COLUMNS of beds, actual transparent background. Row 1 is the original warm wooden bed with white pillow and burgundy red blanket; row 2 is the same bed with blue blanket. Columns are four REDRAWN top-down RPG orientations: 1 headboard at TOP and footboard at BOTTOM; 2 headboard LEFT; 3 headboard BOTTOM and footboard TOP; 4 headboard RIGHT. In column 3 the mattress and blanket MUST remain visible from above across the upper two thirds of the bed; the nearest headboard is short and only covers the bottom third, never a solid wooden panel covering the whole mattress. These are beds viewed from overhead with a little visible vertical face, not upright doors or cupboards. All views share the same wood, simple dark contours and flat three-tone shading, native logical 32x48 or48x32 pixels. Uniform four-column/two-row grid with wide transparent gutters. No floor, glow, shadow, lighting backdrop, text, labels, border or antialiasing. Keep colors and compact handheld pixel-art style of reference.

processing: Grid extraction, alpha threshold190 for hard clean pixel contours, nearest-neighbour downscale, versioned atlas packing. Existing twenty front sprites are copied unchanged; native PC front is reused by its original renderer. Maria uses scale only, same source.
